subject: astronaut on moon
title: There Are 96 Bags of Astronaut Waste on the Moon. Scientists Want Them

scenes.text: Astronauts left 96 bags of waste on the Moon.
Six Apollo crews landed. Before leaving, each one dumped whatever it didn't need for the trip home.
Urine, vomit, leftover food, and yes, that too. All of it bagged and left on the surface.
Less weight in the cabin meant more Moon rock could come back.
Half a century later, scientists want those bags.
They were full of microbes. If anything inside survived fifty years of vacuum and radiation, it changes what we think life can take.

description:
There are 96 bags of human waste on the Moon.
The six Apollo missions that landed left behind bags of urine, feces, vomit and food waste, part of the roughly 400,000 pounds of material humans have left on the lunar surface, often discarded so the weight of Moon rocks would not affect the flight home. Scientists now want to study the bags to learn what half a century on the Moon has done to them, and whether any of the microbes inside could have survived. University of Florida researcher Andrew Schuerger has said survival is highly improbable, but that the bags are the likeliest place for it of anything that landed on the Moon. NASA has no firm plan to retrieve them yet.
Should we bring them back? Comment below.
first_comment: On Apollo 16, nine species of microbes were exposed to open space for a few days, and many survived. Should someone go and get the bags?
